nba_directive.reason_text: This client has a 3.62% rate that almost certainly cannot be beaten in today's market, so a rate-and-term refi would raise their payment — the play is to make the cost of waiting concrete by tying a pinned callback to their stated life goal, while protecting their low first-mortgage rate if any equity need surfaces.
nba_directive.recommended_strategy_text:
- Open by acknowledging their 3.62% rate is a real asset worth protecting
  - Name it explicitly: 'Your 3.62% conventional rate is one of the best in the market — we are not touching that'
  - This builds trust and disarms any fear that you are trying to sell them something harmful

- Make the delay concrete by connecting it to their stated life goal
  - Ask directly if you do not already know: 'What is the financial goal you are working toward — retirement, paying off debt, funding something specific?'
  - Once confirmed, quantify the cost of waiting: calculate how many months of interest accrue on their $422,959 balance at 3.62% while they wait (roughly $1,277/mo in interest at current balance), and frame that as the real price of inaction
  - Example framing: 'Every month we wait, approximately $1,277 of your $2,174 payment is still going to interest — let us make sure any move we make is actually accelerating your goal, not just reacting to rate headlines'

- Reframe what 'waiting for rates' actually means for them
  - Since their rate is 3.62%, a refinance only makes sense if rates drop well below that — walk them through what rate would need to be achieved to lower their $2,174 P&I payment meaningfully
  - Coach the banker: run the amortization at their current balance of $422,959 and show what rate would be required to produce a payment meaningfully below $2,174 — do not invent a number, show the math live or in a follow-up text
  - Reframe: 'Waiting for rates makes sense only if rates drop far enough to beat 3.62% — let us put a number on exactly what that threshold is for you'

- If any equity or debt need exists, introduce a HELOC/second lien as the protective alternative
  - Frame it as leaving their 3.62% first mortgage completely untouched
  - If they carry credit card balances, contrast HELOC rates against the 25–30% they are paying on cards — use their actual balances if known; if not, ask: 'Do you have any high-rate debt we should factor in? Even a partial consolidation could offset the HELOC rate entirely'

- Pin a concrete callback before closing the text
  - Do not accept a vague 'check back later' — offer two specific times: 'Can we do a 10-minute call Tuesday at 10am or Thursday at 2pm to lock in your threshold number so you know exactly when to pull the trigger?'
  - Confirm via text reply and set a calendar reminder to follow through — single-attempt-then-silence is the anti-pattern to avoid

- Close with a low-friction next step
  - 'I will send you a one-page summary showing your current payment breakdown and the exact rate target that would make a refi worth it — just reply YES and I will have it to you within the hour'
